units.source_text: 席上诸人赋诗甚多，为免烦冗，恕不尽述。

en.t: The people at the gathering composed many poems, but to avoid tedious detail, I will not recount them all.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣恣情谈笑，庄谐杂作，众人皆想听他千年，看他万载，真是斧头柄要烂光了。

en.t: The Genji Inner Minister talked and laughed as freely as he pleased, mixing dignity with wit, and everyone wished they could listen to him for a thousand years and gaze on him for ten thousand, until even the handle of an axe would have rotted away.

units.source_text: 但逗留已有四天，今日必须返都。

en.t: But they had already stayed for four days, and today they had to return to the capital.

units.source_text: 便将各种衣服分别赏赐众人。

en.t: So he distributed various garments as gifts to the people there.

units.source_text: 他们把这些衣服搭在肩上，在雾中忽隐忽现，五彩缤纷，望去几疑是庭中的花草，景象异常美观。

en.t: They draped the garments over their shoulders, appearing and disappearing in the mist, so bright with many colors that from a distance they almost seemed like flowers and grasses in the garden, a remarkably beautiful sight.

units.source_text: 近卫府中以擅长神乐、催马乐或东游等歌曲著名的舍人，有几个此时亦随侍在侧。

en.t: Several attendants from the Palace Guards, known for their skill in kagura, saibara, Azuma-asobi, and other songs, were also waiting at his side at this time.

units.source_text: 这些人游兴尚未餍足，便唱着神乐歌《此马》之章，跳起舞来。

en.t: Their pleasure in the outing was still not satisfied, so they sang the 'This Horse' section of a kagura song and began to dance.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣以下，许多人从身上脱下衣服来赏赐他，那些衣服披在肩上，红紫错综，仿佛秋风中翻飞的红叶。

en.t: Beginning with the Genji Inner Minister, many people took off garments from their own bodies and gave them to the dancer; draped over his shoulders, the red and purple robes mingled like crimson leaves whirling in the autumn wind.

units.source_text: 如此大队人马喧嚣扰攘地返京，大堰邸中的人遥闻声息，颇有落寞之感，大家惘然若失。

en.t: As this great company noisily and busily returned to the capital, the people at the Oi residence heard the commotion from afar, felt a deep loneliness, and all were left dazed as though they had lost something.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣不曾再度向明石姬告别，亦觉于心不安。

en.t: The Genji Inner Minister had not gone again to say farewell to the Lady Akashi, and he too felt uneasy about it in his heart.
